text:
Tara (Sales): Polaris Logistics sent over a POC ask: mixed flow (embed lookup -> chat reply). Requirements: sustained 200 QPS for chat, target p50 <= 120ms, occasional spikes to ~700 QPS for 30s, embeddings batched at 8 per request. They also want a simple cost comparison hosted vs dedicated and confirmation on KMS/HSM and audit log behavior. Can we validate next Tue?

Leo (PerfEng): Ack. Need model names & avg token counts. Also: are embeddings done synchronously in the request path or async?

Tara (Sales): Models: chat-lite-v0 (~60 tokens avg) and embed-512s (each input ~256 tokens, batched 8). They do embeddings in the hot path before the chat call.

Priya (SRE): For sustained 200 QPS chat @60 tokens, recommended dedicated: 3x A10-equivalent hosts with continuous batching and prefix cache gives good efficiency. For 700QPS spikes, autoscale warmup + a burst pool (or hosted burst) needed. Note HSM on hot path adds measurable tail latency — I'll quantify.

Owen (Solutions): Quick cost heuristic: hosted unit ~= tokens*$0.00095 + embedding per-batch surcharge; dedicated amortized GPU & infra reduces unit cost by ~40% at commit levels. I'll put numbers into slide once we have test numbers.

Leo (PerfEng): I'll craft a small mixedbench using k6 and a tiny harness: embeddings POST then chat POST, maintain order. Use --rps to shape sustained vs spike windows. Pseudocode:
```
import http from 'k6/http';
export default function() {
  http.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', JSON.stringify({model:'embed-512s', inputs:[...8 times]}));
  http.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat', JSON.stringify({model:'chat-lite-v0', messages:[{role:'user',content:'...'}]}));
}
```
Will share exact script.

Tara (Sales): Polaris prefers hosted first so procurement can exercise audit flow. They asked for explicit numbers on KMS latency (customer-managed key) vs platform-managed.

Priya (SRE): Ran a quick hosted smoke run: 5m sustain at 200RPS. Results: chat p50 135ms, p95 260ms, p99 410ms. Embedding batch p50 85ms. Enabling CMK (customer-managed key) increased chat p50 by ~11ms and p99 by ~28ms in this run. GPU util ~68%, CPU ~40%.

infra-bot: perf-run-3601234567-hosted initiated by Priya at 2026-03-21T13:40:12Z

Leo (PerfEng): Good baseline. For the 700QPS spike test I did a 30s burst on hosted: observed p50 210ms, p95 640ms, p99 1.1s. We need burst pool to keep tails tight.

Owen (Solutions): Draft recommendation: 1) Start hosted POC to validate integration and get procurement/compliance signoff. 2) If Polaris needs predictable unit economics and heavy sustained traffic, switch to Dedicated with reserved pool + burst nodes. 3) HSM can be configured off hot token path to avoid per-token HSM overhead; if they insist on HSM for every key op expect +10-30ms depending on vendor.

Tara (Sales): Can someone attach the raw logs and a one-line summary I can put on an exec slide? Procurement needs the KMS numbers inline.

Priya (SRE): Uploading: https://internal.redwood/polaris/3601234567/hosted-smoke-logs.tar.gz. One-line summary: "Hosted smoke: sustained 200RPS -> chat p50 135ms (CMK +11ms), embedding batch p50 85ms; 30s burst to 700RPS increases chat p99 to ~1.1s; recommend Dedicated for sustained low unit-cost + burst pool for spikes."

Leo (PerfEng): Commands used: `k6 run --duration 5m --rps 200 mixedflow.js` and for burst: `k6 run --duration 2m --vus 800 --rps 700 burst-mixedflow.js`. Bench harness repo: https://git.internal/redwood/bench/mixedflow

Owen (Solutions): I'll translate logs into a 1-slide cost matrix (hosted vs dedicated with commit scenarios) and list security tradeoffs (CMK latency delta, HSM on/off path).

Tara (Sales): Thanks all. I'll send to Polaris and ask their security lead if they need HSM per-request or just key custody/audit. If they need per-token HSM we'll flag the tail impact.

Priya (SRE): Action items: attach grafana panel link, finalize burst run with warmup, and run CMK vs platform-key A/B for a longer window. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/polaris/3601234567

Tara (Sales): Perfect. I'll schedule the exec call and share the slide once Owen posts it. :raised_hands:
